items.author: Loren Blackford, Executive Director
items.title: Sierra Club: BAAJA Remains Fundamentally Flawed Despite Manager’s Amendment
items.summary: Sierra Club said the manager's amendment released Nov. 7 improved the bill but left it flawed, called for an open amendment process, and said it could not support the bill unless more changes were made.

quote.text: The Sierra Club appreciates the improvements made by the manager’s amendment, but the draft legislation remains deeply flawed. The Senate must allow an open amendment process for additional changes to be made.
quote.speaker: Loren Blackford, Executive Director, Sierra Club

items.note: Page read through r.jina.ai; the page dates itself Nov. 8, 2026. Sierra Club's Nov. 6 statement is already held; the Nov. 8 release is not in held_urls.

items.author: Andrew Bowman, president and CEO
items.title: Revised Permitting Bill Fails to Address Threats to Endangered Species Act
items.summary: Defenders of Wildlife said it remained opposed to the bill after the revisions and asked the Senate to reject it and leave negotiations to the next Congress.

quote.text: Defenders of Wildlife remains opposed to the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) following revisions that leave the bill's most damaging provisions affecting the Endangered Species Act largely unchanged.
quote.speaker: Defenders of Wildlife release

items.author: Sambhav Sankar, Senior Vice President of Programs
items.title: The permitting bill will let the Trump administration ignore NEPA
items.summary: Earthjustice's Sankar wrote that Section 1110 limits a court's NEPA remedy to remand without vacatur or injunction and argued that the Administrative Procedure Act would not preserve injunctive relief.

quote.text: Without meaningful judicial remedies, the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) will be virtually impossible to enforce, especially against bad faith actors.
quote.speaker: Sambhav Sankar, Senior Vice President of Programs, Earthjustice

items.note: Earthjustice URL ?p=58002 resolves to the URL given. The earlier-held Earthjustice items are ?p=57975 and ?p=57922; this one is not held.

items.author: Julie Strupp
items.title: Federal permitting bill that could speed apartment construction advances in Senate
items.summary: Multifamily Dive reported that the National Association of Home Builders and YIMBY Action released a letter supporting the bill's housing measures on Nov. 9, and that the National Apartment Association commented on the bill's housing provisions.

quote.text: Industry groups, including the National Association of Home Builders and YIMBY Action, released a letter of support for BAAJA’s housing measures on Monday
quote.speaker: Julie Strupp, Multifamily Dive

people.name: Brian Schatz
people.position: Nov. 9: said he will vote to pass the bill, after changes to the historic preservation title; reacted to the Nov. 7 substitute.

quote.text: While BAAJA is not perfect, it represents a rare opportunity to pass strong, bipartisan legislation that will help lower costs and make it easier for American workers to build the things our country needs. I will vote to pass it

people.note: Primary release; the held Schatz entry rests on The Washington Sun. The release says 'I will vote to pass it' and does not mention amendments.

people.name: Tammy Duckworth
people.position: Nov. 9: announced she would vote against advancing the bill; said the latest committee version was not good enough.

quote.text: While I appreciate some of the changes in the latest version put forward by committee leadership, the bill still isn’t good enough. Not for Illinois, not for the communities who won’t have a say

people.note: Primary release; the held Duckworth entry rests on The Washington Sun.

people.name: Ben Ray Luján
people.position: Nov. 9: said he voted against advancing the bill and could not support advancing it in its current form; no stated position on final passage.

quote.text: After spending the last month listening to these concerns, I cannot support advancing the bill in its current form.

people.note: Primary release; the held Luján entry rests on The Washington Sun.

people.name: John Hickenlooper
people.position: Nov. 9: said he voted to advance the bill, that it is not perfect, and that it should be strengthened with Tribal Nations and environmental groups as it moves through the legislative process.

quote.text: This bill isn’t perfect. No bill is. We should continue working with Tribal Nations and environmental groups to strengthen it as it moves through the legislative process.

people.note: Not in the held people list. The release says the Senate will vote on final passage early the next week; it does not state how he will vote on passage.

rechecks.claim: American Clean Power analysis: BAAJA could unleash 350+ GW of new clean energy, over $800 billion of investment, 290 million metric tons of avoided CO2 annually
rechecks.title: The Clean Energy and Environmental Case for the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (BAAJA)
rechecks.quote: By creating a more predictable path to build, BAAJA can unleash: Over $800 billion in new transmission and clean power infrastructure; 350+ GW of new clean energy;
rechecks.note: URL was real and the figures are on the page, which says 'Resource uploaded Oct. 9, 2026'. The page's third figure reads '290 million metric tons of avoided CO₂ emissions annually — equivalent to the emissions of 63 million cars.' The page states no scenario, baseline or method for any figure and names only 'ACP's latest analysis' (a downloadable fact sheet PDF that was not read). It describes the September 30 text; it predates the November 7 substitute. The figures are ACP's own and no independent model is cited.

rechecks.claim: Public Citizen: Title IV of BAAJA would affect about 39 bcf/d of LNG export capacity
rechecks.title: Senate Permitting Legislation—S. 5653, or BAAJA—Undermines Regulation of Existing LNG Exports, Exposing Consumers To Massive Affordability Harm
rechecks.quote: Title IV of BAAJA directly impedes this Natural Gas Act authority, and will lock in this already-authorized 39 bcf/d of LNG export capacity.
rechecks.note: The figure is on the page but the earlier inferred URL (a /news/ path) returned 404; the page lives at the URL given (citizen.org/?p=128552 redirects to it). It is an analysis piece dated Nov. 8, 2026 (author line not captured by the reader; the search summary names Tyson Slocum). Scenario and baseline: current law, under which the page says the Secretary of Energy can modify export volumes for the 39 bcf/d of authorized exports at existing and under-construction facilities; the page gives the 39 as the sum of 'more 14 billion cubic feet per day' for seven operating facilities and 'the additional 25 bcf/d' commissioned or under construction. It is Public Citizen's claim about Title IV's effect, not a CBO or CRS figure, and it reacts to the Sept. 30 text and the Nov. 7 substitute (the page does not say which).
